### WHY HEXNET IS HELD (do not deploy on the old Chris PASS)
Chris PASSed 916a37ebc. Nancy then returned PAUSE with 4 findings. #1 was stale (she read
the pre-fix file). The other THREE reproduced and Chris had not tested any of them:

1. **TRAINCHECK was memorisable.** Challenge 4 calls `random.seed(s)` in fixed order, so the
   module RNG sat at a known state and TRAINCHECK's draws were byte-identical across
   processes (verified DETERMINISTIC=True) -- while the page told students "randomised every
   run, so memorised weights cannot pass". FIXED: draws from `_tc_rng = random.Random()`
   (OS entropy). Re-verified 3 runs -> 3 different draws.
2. **Challenge 4's claim was cherry-picked -- 3rd unmeasured claim on this one challenge.**
   "zeroed 8/8, leaked <8" holds only on seeds 0-7: fails 12/25 windows, and WIDENING makes
   it worse (24/25 at N=32) since it demands perfection from a ~92% process.
   Measured over 120 seeds: zeroing 110/120 converged, median 0.0082, diverged 0/120;
   leaking 65/120, median 0.0000 (LOWER!), diverged 16/120.
   -> Leaking is NOT slower, it is UNSTABLE. Better lesson, and it is the real reason
   zero_grad exists. Rule is now the comparison `zeroed > leaked` over 16 seeds: 0/20
   window failures. Perfect-score test DELETED, not loosened.
3. **Challenge 1's randomness gate was a source regex** -- failed honest `random.gauss`,
   passed hardcoded weights carrying a dead `random.uniform` call (Nancy built the exploit).
   FIXED: functional two-neuron comparison (`distinct:` / `within_varies:`).

qc-hexnet.sh now gates the SHIPPED rule and hard-fails the build if it breaks.

### GATE 6 -- NANCY'S 7 FINDINGS. DO NOT DEPLOY. Fix in this order.

**#5 IS THE SERIOUS ONE -- THE CENTRAL CLAIM MAY BE FALSE.**
The page teaches that distance-8 recall fails because the gradient signal dies over eight
steps ("nothing left to learn from") -- the textbook vanishing-gradient story, and the
stated reason attention was invented. Nancy trained the shipped config from 40 to 640
steps: TRAINING loss converges smoothly to 0.015 (the net nearly perfectly FITS its 12
training sequences at distance 8) while held-out accuracy stays flat at 12.5%. That is
OVERFITTING a 12-example budget covering a sliver of 4^8 filler combinations -- NOT
gradient starvation. Both motivate attention, but the page asserts the specific
mechanism as measured fact and the measurement does not support it.
=> Either isolate the two effects (vary training-set size at fixed distance; check
   gradient norms at step 1 vs step 8) and teach whichever the data supports, or drop
   the mechanism claim and teach only the observed failure. DO NOT guess again.

**#1 THE HEADLINE NUMBER CONTRADICTS WHAT EVERY STUDENT SEES.** Challenge 4 hardcodes
score_at(1,1) and score_at(8,1). Pyodide is real CPython (WASM), so the RNG is
bit-identical -- every student sees far=58%, deterministically, forever. The prose leads
with "32%... barely above guessing" and frames a higher far score as bad luck they MIGHT
hit. It is not luck, it is certain. Third recurrence of "measured the wrong sample" on
this one page. QC never runs the actual shipped call site.

**#3 CHALLENGE 4 STILL HAS THE ABSOLUTE BAR I REMOVED FROM CHALLENGE 3.** `near >= 0.6`,
unpaired. Nancy measured false-fail 3/40 (7.5%) on CORRECT builds. QC measures the two
margin rules but never this one -- a gap against the script's own stated doctrine. Inert
today only because the hardcoded seed clears it.

**#2 CHALLENGE 2 GIVES FULL MARKS TO THE BUG THIS GATE EXISTS TO FIX.** A forward() that
reads only seq[-1] -- no memory at all, exactly Gate 5's one-character limit -- scores
4/4, because the order test hardcodes [0,1,2] vs [2,1,0] whose LAST elements differ.
Deterministic, 100% reproducible.

**#4** the disclosed "12%-58%" spread is checked by nothing; her 40-seed resample gives
8%-54%. min/max are unstable and widen with N.
**#6** runtime measured only in CPython (0.65s/3.67s). Students run Pyodide; never
measured there. Could be 15-45s for challenge 4. The doctrine comment calls runtime a
controlled constraint, then does not control it.
**#7** challenge 1's "bounded by tanh" passes for a fully LINEAR cell -- small init
lands in range by luck, not construction.

VERIFIED CLEAN by Nancy: untouched starter 0/14 all four challenges; structurally
different correct solutions pass; a no-zero-grad train loop correctly fails; QC's own
adversarial cheats rejected; qc-hexmemory.sh passes end to end.

### CHRIS BLOCK -- 3 MORE, and he reproduced a LIVE FAILURE on the committed file

**C1 THE GATE IS FLAKY AND I SHIPPED "QC 4/4" ON ONE LUCKY SAMPLE.** Chris ran
qc-hexmemory.sh against a byte-identical copy of HEAD (diff empty, zero edits) and got
"false-fail 'far memory is gone': 1/12  GATE FAILED". A rerun seconds later passed.
Root cause he isolated: accuracy is measured on n=24 held-out examples, so it QUANTIZES
to ~4.17-point steps, and the strict >= / < comparisons sitting exactly at the 25-point
boundary are reachable by chance. At n=48 seeds he measured 1/48 (~2.1%) on BOTH the
paired rule and the margin rule, from the same tie-boundary seed (5015: before 58.3%,
after 58.3%, exact tie). So "measured 0/12" is not elimination, it is a small sample.
=> Fix: widen the boundary with a documented epsilon or bump the margin, AND replace
   "0/12" with the honest residual rate at a larger sample.

**C2 THE +/-18pp TOLERANCE IS UNDER-SAMPLED, WHICH IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION.**
Not theatre -- he poisoned "distance 4 -> 57%" to 99% and it correctly failed. But QC
verifies each distance from only 3 fresh seeds. Bootstrapping 2000 3-seed draws against
the page's own (correct) values gives self-inflicted false-fail 1.8% / 6.4% / 4.0% /
0.4% -- roughly a 1-in-8 chance that ANY rerun reports a phantom FAIL on a correct page.
=> Fix: raise to n>=12 per distance so the self-inflicted rate drops under 1%.

**C3 PYODIDE RUNTIME WAS NEVER MEASURED.** The doctrine comment calls runtime "a design
constraint, not an afterthought" and then cites CPython only, with "Pyodide is slower"
as an assumption. Chris built a real headless-Chromium + Pyodide 0.25.1 harness:
distance 1 = 0.86s, distance 8 = 4.21s, ~5.1s combined. The design is FINE -- but it
shipped unverified, and the gap resolved in my favour by luck. Also: no Web Worker, so
that ~5s is a synchronous main-thread freeze worth disclosing.
=> Fix: put the real numbers in the comment; note the freeze.

**WHERE NANCY AND CHRIS DIVERGE -- resolve before rewriting challenge 4.**
Chris's independent 60-seed sweep CORROBORATES the page figures (94/77/57/32, deviations
0.7-4.4pp; d8 mean 27.6% sd 9.3) and he calls the decay real and the "barely above
guessing" framing correct. Nancy does NOT dispute the decay -- she disputes the stated
MECHANISM (vanishing gradient) versus overfitting a 12-example set. Both can be true:
the phenomenon is real, my explanation of WHY may be wrong. Settle it by isolating the
two -- vary training-set size at fixed distance, and inspect gradient magnitude at step
1 vs step 8 -- then teach whichever the data supports.

CONTEXT NOTE: these were NOT fixed because the session ran out of context. Fixing 7
findings -- one of which needs a fresh measurement campaign to settle overfitting vs

### GATE 6 -- MEASUREMENTS DONE, DO NOT RE-DERIVE
Spec (01-SOURCE-PROPOSAL.md:37): "Representation and sequence learning (RNN/LSTM, why
attention emerged)". The gate rests on ONE claim, and it is textbook conventional wisdom
of exactly the kind that FAILED measurement twice in Gate 3. So it was measured first.

TASK DESIGN: sequence = [cue, filler x distance]; model must reproduce the cue symbol.
VOCAB=4, HID=8, squared error on one-hot, lr 0.3, 40 steps, 12 train / 24 fresh test.
RNN: h_t = tanh(Wxh x_t + Whh h_{t-1} + b), output = Why h_T. Runs on the HexGrad Value
engine, so it composes with Gates 2-3 rather than importing anything.

THE CLAIM HOLDS, and harder than expected (chance = 25%):
  distance 1 -> 90%   distance 2 -> 83%   distance 4 -> 46%   distance 8 -> 40%
GRADED RULE 'near(d=1) > far(d=8)' measured over 12 seeds:
  held 12/12, ties 0/12; near mean 91% vs far mean 24%; near MIN 62% vs far MAX 50%
  (clean separation, no overlap); margin min +38%, mean +67%
=> At distance 8 the RNN scores 24% against a 25% chance baseline. The memory is not
   degraded, it is GONE. That is the honest, measured reason attention was invented,
   and it is a far better lesson than asserting "RNNs forget".

FEASIBILITY (blocking question, answered): CPython 0.6s (d=1) to 3.4s (d=8) per full
train+score. Pyodide is slower, so keep d<=8, steps<=40, and warn the learner that the
long-distance run takes a moment. Do NOT scale VOCAB or HID up without re-timing.

  every check has a not-found guard (Nancy found one silently checking nothing),

- Write the ContentCatalog entry BY HAND. Copy-pasting the sibling entry shipped
  HexToken's description onto Gate 5, and no gate reads ContentCatalog -- nothing
  catches it.
- Poison-test every gate and VERIFY THE POISON LANDED before trusting the result.
  Strings span JS concat breaks; a naive sed silently no-ops and reads as a gate defect.
- Parallel agents on the shared tree collide (Chris hit this). Use a worktree.

FILED, NOT DROPPED: (1) no duplicate-description validator exists for ContentCatalog --

### GATE 5 (HexTalk) -- MEASURED FACTS, do not re-derive
Corpus = 3 sentences, vocab 27.
- Uniform perplexity = 27.00, EXACTLY the vocab size. Strong teaching fact.
- Bigram (add-1 smoothing) perplexity = 10.75 -> measured 2.51x better than uniform.

TEMPERATURE -- first metric was WRONG, second works:
- distinct-character count shows NO effect (26.8 vs 27.0 across temps 0.3-1.5). The
  metric SATURATES over a few hundred samples. Do not use it, and do not claim
  "low temp = more repetitive" on that basis.
- real-bigram share (fraction of sampled pairs that occur in the corpus) works, large
  and monotonic:  temp 0.2 -> 97.9% | 0.5 -> 49.4% | 1.0 -> 23.1% | 2.0 -> 15.6% | 5.0 -> 13.2%
- top-char share also works: 22.9% -> 12.7% -> 7.1% -> 5.9% -> 5.9%
- entropy works but saturates above temp 1.0 (3.24 -> 3.25), weaker signal.
THE CLAIM TO TEACH: low temperature makes the model play SAFE, reusing pairs it actually
saw; high temperature makes it INVENT pairs it never saw. Measured, not assumed.
Probes: scratchpad/hexnet/{bigram_probe,temp_probe}.py

BUILD RULE FOR GATE 5, learned the hard way in Gate 3: measure against the EXACT code
